base: Would be: Ownly first-time users in Gachibowli
formula: D30 repeat rate (%) x average 30-day order frequency among retained users
data_source: Ownly transaction logs — not available to this study
why_good_indicator: It is the only metric that answers the actual question — does a cheaper first order become a habit. DoorDash reports the same construct publicly (cohort retention x frequency), and Rapido's own co-founder has said affordability is meant to drive repeat, frequency and retention rather than GOV. Awareness and trial are upstream proxies; this is the outcome.
limitation: Requires per-user transaction history. No survey question can substitute — stated intent is not behaviour.
what_would_upgrade_it: Ownly cohort export: first-order date, subsequent order dates, per user.
family: North Star — D30 Retained Order Rate

formula: baskets where Ownly final payable is lowest / all matched baskets
why_good_indicator: The structural position: what Ownly's price looks like before any incumbent benefit applies. This is the version Ownly controls.
limitation: n=4 matched baskets, one slot, one address. Ownly on a new account with an intro offer; incumbents on subscribed accounts.
what_would_upgrade_it: More restaurants, a second slot, and a membership-holding Ownly account.

formula: baskets where Ownly final payable is lowest / all matched baskets
why_good_indicator: What a Swiggy One or Zomato Gold holder actually sees. Since 82.5% of this catchment holds a membership, this is most people's real checkout.
limitation: n=4 matched baskets, one slot, one address. Ownly on a new account with an intro offer; incumbents on subscribed accounts.
what_would_upgrade_it: More restaurants, a second slot, and a membership-holding Ownly account.

formula: baskets where Ownly final payable is lowest / all matched baskets
why_good_indicator: What happens when a coupon lands. This is the version that decides whether the price advantage survives a competitive response.
limitation: n=4 matched baskets, one slot, one address. Ownly on a new account with an intro offer; incumbents on subscribed accounts.
what_would_upgrade_it: More restaurants, a second slot, and a membership-holding Ownly account.

formula: median(cheapest incumbent final payable - Ownly final payable), list+fees view
why_good_indicator: Converts the price claim into rupees, which is the unit the switching-threshold question is also measured in — so the two can be compared directly.
limitation: Before any incumbent coupon or membership benefit.
what_would_upgrade_it: Expanded matched-basket audit.

kpi_name: Fee Load — non-food share of bill
formula: (packaging+platform+delivery+small cart+surge+GST) / final payable
why_good_indicator: The one advantage Ownly controls outright. Unlike a discount it survives without subsidy, so it is the durable half of the price story. Incumbent median is 23.4%.
limitation: Median across priced captures; excludes menu-price differences.
what_would_upgrade_it: Capture across dayparts to confirm no surge is applied at peak.

base: Catchment respondents naming a rupee figure (n=33); 4 said no amount, 3 don't know
formula: median of stated recurring saving needed to change main app
why_good_indicator: Defines the bar Ownly's price advantage has to clear. Paired with the observed saving it becomes Switch-Threshold Coverage (MM3), which is the most decision-relevant metric here.
limitation: Stated threshold, not observed switching. 'No amount' and 'don't know' are held out of the median and reported separately rather than coded as zero or infinity.
what_would_upgrade_it: Behavioural test: vary the discount and observe actual switching.

formula: restaurants listed on Ownly / restaurants in the audit frame
data_source: Price audit (thu_lunch pass excluded, rule R4)
why_good_indicator: Assortment is the attribute respondents refused to trade for money, so coverage is the constraint most likely to cap adoption.
limitation: This is AUDIT-FRAME coverage, NOT Gachibowli market coverage. The frame was built from Ownly's own showcase page plus incumbent chains, so it selects for restaurants present everywhere and cannot detect exclusives.
what_would_upgrade_it: A long-tail pass: 25-30 restaurants sampled from Ownly's own 221-item list, checked on Swiggy and Zomato.

formula: restaurants on Ownly AND >=1 incumbent / restaurants on Ownly
why_good_indicator: Directly tests the 'no new use case' risk that killed earlier challengers: if the catalogue is the same, price is the only differentiator left.
limitation: Frame of 10. 1 Ownly-only and 1 missing-from-Ownly observed.
what_would_upgrade_it: Long-tail coverage pass.

base: Would be: respondents' own most-ordered restaurants
formula: respondents' top/last-used restaurants available on Ownly / their top restaurants
data_source: Survey does not capture named restaurants
why_good_indicator: Generic coverage counts restaurants; this counts the ones a person actually uses. Because 61.8% will not trade their usual restaurants for ₹30, this is the version of coverage that predicts behaviour.
limitation: The live instrument never asks respondents to name their usual restaurants.
what_would_upgrade_it: Add one question: 'name the 3 places you order from most', then check each on Ownly.

formula: median(Ownly quoted ETA) - median(incumbent quoted ETA)
why_good_indicator: Quantifies what the saving costs in time. The gap is flat across all four restaurants (+17.5 to +24 min), which is the signature of a supply-density problem rather than a logistics one — see H-OUTLET.
limitation: QUOTED ETA, not delivery performance. No test orders were placed, so on-time rate is unknown.
what_would_upgrade_it: 3 test orders recording promised vs actual; and outlet name/distance per platform.

formula: orders delivered within promised ETA / total orders; and cancellation rate
data_source: Requires placed orders or platform data
why_good_indicator: Interviews say people leave an app after repeated bad orders, so fulfilment reliability is the retention guardrail. A quoted ETA cannot measure it.
limitation: The 3 budgeted test orders were never placed; template is empty.
what_would_upgrade_it: Place the 3 test orders; or obtain Ownly's on-time and cancellation rates.

base: Would be: Rapido users exposed to the Ownly entry point
formula: Ownly first orders / Rapido users exposed to the Ownly entry point
why_good_indicator: Tests whether the distribution advantage converts, which is the single biggest claimed asset of the Ownly model. Uber Eats had the same amortised-fleet logic and it did not save it.
limitation: No exposure or browse data exists outside Rapido.
what_would_upgrade_it: Rapido: impressions of the food entry point -> browse -> first order.

formula: noticed food inside the Rapido app / Rapido users ('Not sure' counted as not noticed)
why_good_indicator: Rapido's user base is the cheapest acquisition asset Ownly has. This separates access (they are in the app) from discovery (they noticed the product). Interviews say trial actually comes from friends and creators, not placement — so this tests the assumption.
limitation: Self-reported noticing, subject to recall.
what_would_upgrade_it: In-app exposure-to-first-order analytics from Rapido.

formula: top-2 box on 'once the ₹100 first-order offer ended, would you keep using it'
why_good_indicator: The closest available stand-in for the North Star. It asks the rented-demand question directly: does the behaviour survive the subsidy. Foodpanda went from ~200k to ~5k daily orders when discounts stopped, so this is the failure mode worth measuring.
limitation: STATED INTENT, not retention. People overstate future good behaviour.
what_would_upgrade_it: Observed second-order rate among promo-acquired users.

formula: agree + strongly agree that a new app's low prices rise once it becomes popular
why_good_indicator: A price proposition only works if it is believed. This measures whether the market has already priced in the fee creep it has seen from every previous challenger.
limitation: Attitudinal. Does not by itself predict behaviour.
what_would_upgrade_it: Test whether doubt predicts non-trial in a behavioural experiment.

formula: revenue per order - variable delivery, payment and support cost per order
why_good_indicator: The guardrail that separates growth from burn. Uber Eats India lost $2.55 per order against a $2.45 average order value — it lost more per order than the order was worth. Any repeat rate is meaningless without this. Our audit observed Ownly charging ₹0 delivery, ₹0 platform and ₹0 packaging while taking 0% commission, so observed revenue per order in Gachibowli was ₹0.
limitation: Ownly has never published per-order economics; no figure exists in any source.
what_would_upgrade_it: Ownly internal: revenue and variable cost per order.

formula: has_membership = true / respondents answering
why_good_indicator: Members never see Ownly's list-price advantage — a membership converts a structural saving into no saving at all. It is the single largest barrier measured in this study.
limitation: Membership held, not necessarily used.
what_would_upgrade_it: Larger sample; confirm active use of the membership.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: multihoming = true / respondents answering
why_good_indicator: A multi-homing market lets Ownly become a secondary app before it becomes a main one, which is a lower bar than switching. It also means trial does not imply displacement.
limitation: Based on self-reported 4-week order counts.
what_would_upgrade_it: Larger sample; confirm active use of the membership.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: ownly_aware / all catchment respondents
why_good_indicator: Top of funnel. Ownly is weeks old in Hyderabad, so this is the ceiling on everything downstream.
limitation: Self-reported. Trial base is very small.
what_would_upgrade_it: Larger sample; Ownly's own first-order counts for the pincode.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: ownly_opened / all catchment respondents
why_good_indicator: Stronger than awareness — it is an action, and it separates 'heard of it' from 'looked at it'.
limitation: Self-reported. Trial base is very small.
what_would_upgrade_it: Larger sample; Ownly's own first-order counts for the pincode.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: ownly_says_ordered / all catchment respondents
why_good_indicator: The first behavioural step. Low base, so reported as directional.
limitation: Self-reported. Trial base is very small.
what_would_upgrade_it: Larger sample; Ownly's own first-order counts for the pincode.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: sum of self-reported Ownly orders in the last 4 weeks
why_good_indicator: Would be the cleanest adoption signal available without company data.
limitation: 1 respondents said they had ordered on Ownly AND that their first order was within the last 4 weeks, while entering 0 orders for that same window. Those fields contradict each other, so the count is reported as UNAVAILABLE rather than as zero adoption. The 4-week window also mostly predates Ownly's Hyderabad go-live (NRAI launch 22 Jul 2026; on-ground September 2026), so a zero here would measure the question window, not rejection.
what_would_upgrade_it: Ask recent-order count with an explicit 'since Ownly launched here' anchor.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: chose the ₹230 option over ₹260 / respondents answering
why_good_indicator: Holds ₹30 constant and varies only what is given up, so differences are attributable to the attribute rather than to price sensitivity. Tests whether users will wait 15 minutes longer.
limitation: Constructed choice at a single price point; not observed behaviour.
what_would_upgrade_it: Repeat at ₹20/₹50/₹75 to build a trade-off curve.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: chose the ₹230 option over ₹260 / respondents answering
why_good_indicator: Holds ₹30 constant and varies only what is given up, so differences are attributable to the attribute rather than to price sensitivity. Tests whether users will accept 3-in-10 late instead of 1-in-10.
limitation: Constructed choice at a single price point; not observed behaviour.
what_would_upgrade_it: Repeat at ₹20/₹50/₹75 to build a trade-off curve.
family: Supporting measures — market conditions and funnel

formula: chose the ₹230 option over ₹260 / respondents answering
why_good_indicator: Holds ₹30 constant and varies only what is given up, so differences are attributable to the attribute rather than to price sensitivity. Tests whether users will give up most usual restaurants.
limitation: Constructed choice at a single price point; not observed behaviour.
what_would_upgrade_it: Repeat at ₹20/₹50/₹75 to build a trade-off curve.
